svg.title: Device Authorization Grant
svg.desc: Device Authorization Grant. Sign in on a TV or CLI by approving a short code on your phone. Step 1, Ask for a code: The TV sends its client_id and scope, and gets a secret device_code plus the user code WDJB-MJHT. Step 2, Approve on the phone: The user enters WDJB-MJHT on the phone, signs in with MFA and approves. The TV never sees passwords. Step 3, The TV polls: Meanwhile the TV polls /token: pending, a slow_down that adds 5 s, then access and refresh tokens. Step 4, Other endings, phishing: A denial or a 15-minute expiry ends the flow. The risk: a phished user approves an attacker's code.

g.text: The TV sends its client_id and scope, and gets a secret device_code plus the user code WDJB-MJHT.
The user enters WDJB-MJHT on the phone, signs in with MFA and approves. The TV never sees passwords.
Meanwhile the TV polls /token: pending, a slow_down that adds 5 s, then access and refresh tokens.
A denial or a 15-minute expiry ends the flow. The risk: a phished user approves an attacker's code.
slow_down too soon: wait 10 s from now on
every 10 s until the user approves
times: seconds after the code was issued
device_code: long, random, kept secret by the TV
user_code: short, for a person to type
No client secret: the TV app is a public client
The password and MFA go only to example.com:
The token endpoint answers from the row's status:
consent names the app and device, and warns
only clients that need it may use this grant
lure: “enter QXKT-BHMZ at example.com/device to keep your account”
